manifest.name: dsh-wsl-workspace
manifest.description: WSL workspace support for DeepSeek Harness: add a WSL workspace from the web GUI and run the whole agent session (bash + file tools) inside the WSL distribution, VS Code Remote-WSL style. No toolchain install inside WSL required. Works on DSH Desktop as well as dsh web.

bundle.text:
# dsh-wsl-workspace bundle patch: inserts the host row into the profile's plugin
# roster. The browser half rides the package's `dsh.client` manifest (the client
# registry serves lib/client.js), and the host row materializes the `wsl` agent
# preset on boot. Install with `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <path-or-git-url>`.
- insert:
    - id: wsl-workspace
      name: 'dsh-wsl-workspace'

readme.text: > **Repository-only paths.** This package publishes `lib/`, `cordis.patch.yml`, both READMEs, `TESTING.md`, both CHANGELOGs, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `docs/driving.*` (plus `docs/README.md`, which npm packs because it is named `README`). Paths under `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `ci/` and the rest of `docs/` exist in the repository and are **not published** — this file names them as coordinates, not as files you can open from the tarball.

Add a WSL workspace from the DeepSeek Harness web GUI and run the whole agent session — bash commands and file reads/writes — inside a local WSL distribution with Linux paths. Nothing needs to be installed inside WSL. The session can reach both WSL and Windows at the same time: bash commands run inside the WSL distribution, while Windows files stay accessible via `/mnt/<drive>` (for example `/mnt/c/Users/...`).

Pick one of the three ways below, then restart `dsh web`:

```powershell

readme.section: 2) GitHub repository (ships the prebuilt lib/, no local build required)

readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile web add D:\path\to\dsh-wsl-workspace
```

After restarting `dsh web`, a W button appears in the Workspaces section header, immediately right of the add-workspace control; the collapsed rail keeps it beside Settings at the sidebar foot.

This build declares these DSH releases, each verified on an isolated instance (its own `DSH_HOME`, dependencies pinned to that release, the full check suite):

`0.1.0-rc.7` · `0.1.0-rc.8` · `0.1.1-rc.1` · `0.1.1-rc.2` · `0.1.2-rc.1` · `0.1.3-alpha.2` · `0.1.5-rc.1` · `0.1.5-rc.2` · `0.1.7-rc.1` · `0.1.7-rc.2` · `0.2.0-rc.2` · `0.2.1-rc.2`

The list mirrors `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` in `package.json`, and a unit test fails if the two drift apart. `0.2.1-rc.2` is the DSH release DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` ships — verified against the host inside that application's own bundle, not only against the npm release — so the Desktop is covered by the same declaration; the app's help panel (the dialog's "?" button) shows the same chips next to the plugin version. The plugin detects the DSH generation at runtime and picks the matching API, and a release exposing neither fails loudly instead of leaving an empty workspace. A release outside the list usually still works, but is unverified.

Click that W button — or pick “Add WSL workspace”, directly under “Add workspace…” in the same control’s menu — to open the "Add WSL workspace" dialog. Pick a distribution from the list, then browse the directory tree or type an absolute Linux path (for example `/home/me/proj`) — use the Check button to verify the path exists before creating the workspace. The dialog follows the DeepSeek Harness UI language. The username field is optional: leave it empty to run commands as the distribution's default user, or name a Linux user of that distribution to run the session as that user instead (equivalent to `wsl.exe -u <username>`). The username only changes the bash tool's run identity — the file tools go through the Windows-side WSL share and are unaffected. Each workspace's username is kept in `<dshHome>/wsl-workspaces.json`; delete the entry (or recreate the workspace from the dialog) to return to the default user.

Click "Create & open" to start a new session in the workspace. In the new session the bash tool executes commands inside the chosen distribution and `read`/`write`/`edit` operate on WSL files, so every path the model sees is a Linux path. The mode picker keeps working as usual: Standard, PTC, Minimal and Creative each land on their WSL variant automatically (the WSL variant entries in the picker are bilingual, e.g. `WSL · Standard mode（标准模式）`), and Windows files stay reachable from inside the session under `/mnt/<drive>` (for example `/mnt/c/Users/...`). The dialog's "?" button opens a panel with the DSH releases this build declares, how the plugin is used, and the limitations it cannot fix.

- **bash tool**: runs inside the WSL distribution as the configured username (empty = the distro default user, often `root`), so it can read and write anywhere in the distro. The Windows ACL sandbox cannot wrap `wsl.exe` — its children run on the Linux kernel side — so WSL itself is the isolation boundary and the DSH file policy does not apply to bash.
- **File tools (`read`/`write`/`edit`)**: go through the Windows-side WSL 9P share; the username field does not affect them. Two seams the host's own provider would supply are re-established inside the WSL world, because a variant mounts this plugin's `fs` provider in the preset's isolate realm where the host's `fs-sandbox` wrapper is not in the call path. **Symlinks**: the share lists a Linux link but cannot resolve it, so a link path used to look like a missing file; `resolve`/`lstat` now ask the distribution (`wsl.exe … readlink -f`) and continue at the real path, and a link is never replaced by a regular file. **The access mode**: `write`/`edit` are fenced by `ctx.sandboxPolicy` exactly as the host backend fences them — the same `writableRoots` allow-list (plus the distribution's `/tmp`, the temp area of the world the session run

[docs/driving.md](docs/driving.md) (**ships inside the package**) answers the five questions a fresh agent cannot invent: how to start a harness headlessly (and the one environment variable that must be unset, or the launch exits 0 silently), where the login URL and its token come from (measured: the token is not consumed while that process lives — restart the instance to invalidate it), this plugin's route plus how to enumerate its methods at runtime (`describe`), how to inject text into the composer and send it (the composer is Lexical: one `beforeinput`, never `execCommand`), and how to move a session off a provider that answers 401. The same facts are returned by the plugin's `describe` method (`route`, `loopbackOnly`, `methods`, `installProof`, `driving`), so they travel with the HTTP surface too.

**Most of `docs/` is repository-only** (it is not in `package.json#files`; the shipped files are [docs/driving.md](docs/driving.md), [docs/driving.zh.md](docs/driving.zh.md) and [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), which npm packs because it is named `README`). In the repository, [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) indexes what lives where and in which language: the [design record](docs/design.zh.md) (zh), the [per-release compatibility evidence](docs/compatibility-evidence.md) behind the `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` declaration, and the [archived](docs/archive/) notes whose banners name what superseded them. Before a change or a release, follow [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

- **Adapted/inherited source code**: DeepSeek Harness (MIT) — `dsh-bash-local` (executor mechanics), `dsh-fs-local` (`WslFileSystem` subclasses it), and the shipped agent presets (read and transformed by the variant generator);
- **Design references (no source copied)**: [dsh-bash-terminal](https://github.com/MAXeaglet/dsh-bash-terminal) (MIT, wsl argv / WSLENV approach), [dsh-side-panel](https://github.com/ccq1/dsh-side-panel) (BSD-3-Clause, host-route pattern), [vpshub](https://github.com/Sdongmaker/vpshub) (MIT, roadmap reference).

Special thanks to [dsh-deep-whale](https://github.com/Small-tailqwq/dsh-deep-whale) (DSH Web 鲸鱼娘 skin series · 深海女仆工坊 maid-atelier, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0): the whale girl skin plugin brings a full set of adorable skins to the DeepSeek Harness Web UI and makes daily use of DSH a warmer experience.
